subject: Partial region fallback misfire — eligibility and trace bundle
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@zephyr.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial region degradation — saw timeouts in us-west during morning window

Hi Neha,

We saw elevated 502/504 errors and client-side timeouts for a subset of our checkout traffic hitting us-west between 09:14–09:37 UTC this morning (approx 23 minutes). This affected roughly 2% of requests for our production key (key: ZPH-PROD-9). Our telemetry recorded increased tail latency and a number of failed webhook deliveries.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood recorded an availability gap in us-west for that window?
- If so, whether that qualifies under the SLA for a credit (our contract references 99.95% monthly availability)?
- What evidence you can provide (traces, routing snapshots, autoscaler events) and an ETA for a post-incident report?

We'd like to open a claim but want to align on the window first so we can include accurate impact numbers in our procurement process.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our payments rollout.

Best,
Ellen Park
Director, Engineering
Zephyr Financial

Attachment: none
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@zephyr.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial region degradation — saw timeouts in us-west during morning window

Hi Ellen — thanks for the heads up and the specific window.

We're starting a focused triage now. Initial answers:
- I don't yet have the final availability calculation, but our ingress metrics show a spike in 5xx for the us-west model pool in that timeframe.
- We'll pull traces and request routing snapshots, autoscaler logs, and eviction events to validate whether this meets the SLA breach threshold.

Can you confirm the API key (you mentioned ZPH-PROD-9) and share any request IDs or sample timestamps for failed calls (if you captured any)? That will help speed the evidence match.

I'll loop in our infra team (Aditya) and ops (Grace) and get you an initial evidence bundle within 48 hours and a target postmortem timeline. If eligible, we'll propose the pro-rata credit and the mechanics for applying it to your account.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll treat this as priority.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: ACTION: Zephyr Financial — us-west availability spike (09:14–09:37 UTC) — collect evidence and calc eligibility

Team — escalating: Zephyr Financial reported a ~23 minute window of elevated 502/504 and timeouts in us-west (customer key ZPH-PROD-9). Their contract references 99.95% monthly availability.

What I need from each of you by EOD Monday (US-PST):
- Aditya: routing_snapshot for us-west for 2028-06-22 09:00–10:00 UTC; autoscaler events and any node eviction/oom logs for the model pool that hosts their pinned variant.
- Grace: availability calc for the customer-facing tiers (per our SLA buckets) for June month-to-date and an initial credit estimate table (pro-rata).
- Marissa: start the postmortem draft template and capture the timeline; set the postmortem owner and ack to the customer that we'll deliver within 10 business days.

Preliminary theory from metrics: short-lived spike accompanied by a mismatch in fallback policy that prevented automatic routing to the warm fallback pool. If true, that increases eligibility for an SLA remedy.

Mark any sensitive logs with redaction flags; we'll only share necessary artifacts. Attachments to gather: traces.ndjson, routing_snapshot.csv, node_events.log.

Thanks — Neha

Attachment: none
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACTION: Zephyr Financial — us-west availability spike (09:14–09:37 UTC)

Quick update / evidence bundle attached (redacted where applicable):
- traces-20280622.ndjson (sampled traces tied to ZPH-PROD-9 request ids)
- routing_snapshot-us-west-20280622.csv (shows in-flight routing table + fallback rules)
- node_events-eviction.log (two short-lived preemptions observed at 09:13:24 and 09:16:08 UTC)

Findings summary:
- At 09:13 UTC a transient eviction reduced healthy capacity in the primary pool by ~12%.
- The fallback policy for that pool had an unexpected predicate (legacy config) that prevented routing to the warm-fallback group for ~2 minutes, resulting in a window where requests hit underprovisioned hosts and saw elevated latencies/5xx.
- Autoscaler responded and capacity recovered by ~09:37 UTC.

Proposed immediate customer-facing actions:
1) Confirm SLA window: 09:14:20–09:36:55 UTC (23m 35s) — support will provide exact per-customer impact table.
2) Recommend pro-rata credit per contract: based on our SLA formula this window crosses the monthly threshold; preliminary credit calc attached (sla_credit_worksheet.xlsx).
3) Long-term fix: remove legacy predicate, add unit test to fallback policy, and add alerting on fallback-miss metric (engineering action).

I'll push the artifacts to the secure share and redact PII. Grace — can you run the credit calc and confirm exact amount to offer? Marissa — please set the postmortem owner and timeline.

- Aditya

Attachment: traces-20280622.ndjson, routing_snapshot-us-west-20280622.csv, node_events-eviction.log, sla_credit_worksheet.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@zephyr.com>, Zach Emerson <zach.emerson@zephyr.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial region fallback misfire — eligibility and trace bundle

Hi Ellen and Zach — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and next steps below.

1) Confirmed window and eligibility
- Confirmed impacted window (Redwood metrics): 2028-06-22 09:14:20–09:36:55 UTC (23 minutes, 35 seconds).
- Cause: transient node evictions in the primary us-west pool combined with a legacy fallback predicate that prevented automatic routing to the warm-fallback pool for a ~2 minute sub-window.
- Eligibility: Under the terms of our SLA (99.95% monthly availability), the measured outage crosses the contract threshold for June and therefore qualifies for a pro-rata service credit.

2) Evidence provided (attached)
- traces-20280622.ndjson (sample traces tied to your API key)
- routing_snapshot-us-west-20280622.csv (routing table + fallback config at time)
- node_events-eviction.log (eviction events showing reduced capacity)
- sla_credit_worksheet.xlsx (workbook with the pro-rata calcula tion and proposed credit)

3) Proposed remedy and timeline
- Credit: We propose applying a pro-rata credit equal to 0.6% of June service fees for the affected endpoints (worksheet details the math). If you'd prefer a fixed dollar credit, we can convert that figure on request.
- Postmortem: Deliverable due within 10 business days (owner: Marissa Cole). The postmortem will include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and regression protections.
- Follow-up: Engineering will remove the legacy fallback predicate and add a unit test and alerting for fallback-miss within the next sprint.

4) Acceptance and next steps
- If you accept the pro-rata credit, reply with confirmation and we'll apply it to invoice INV-202806 for your account.
- If you need additional artifacts (raw traces, expanded log windows), let us know and we'll provide them under the secure share link.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand the rollout impact and will prioritize preventing a recurrence.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: traces-20280622.ndjson, routing_snapshot-us-west-20280622.csv, node_events-eviction.log, sla_credit_worksheet.xlsx
